title: First detection of the pre-biotic molecule glycolonitrile (HOCH<SUB>2</SUB>CN) in the interstellar medium
question: Is glycolonitrile (HOCH2CN) present in the ISM toward the Solar-type protostar IRAS16293-2422 B, what are its excitation temperatures and abundances, and can gas-grain chemical modelling reproduce them?

evidence.quote: An H$_2$ column density of N(H$_2$)=2.8$\times$10$^{25}$ cm$^{-2}$ was adopted from (cite: martin-domenech_detection_2017)
an H$_2$ column density of N(H$_2$)=1.5$\times$10$^{23}$ cm$^{-2}$ was adopted using the envelope profile constrained by (cite: crimier2010)

what.value: HOCH2CN spectroscopy from CDMS based on laboratory work

evidence.quote: we have used the spectroscopic parameters from the Cologne Database for Molecular Spectroscopy (CDMS)

external_data.citation: (cite: muller_cologne_2001; muller_cologne_2005; endres_cologne_2016); lab work (cite: margules_submillimeter_2017)

recipe.goal: Calibrate and image archival data, extract spectra
recipe.method: Standard calibration scripts and CASA; uv-plane continuum subtraction; spectra extracted in a 1.6" diameter circle at I16293B

recipe.goal: Identify HOCH2CN lines and fit LTE synthetic spectra
recipe.method: MADCUBA-SLIM synthetic LTE spectra with opacity, manual adjustment then MADCUBA-AUTOFIT; two temperature components
key_parameters: Free: Ntot, Tex, VLSR, linewidth; cold component linewidth fixed to 1 km/s; warm source size 0.5", cold >20"

recipe.method: Two linear least-squares fits to E_up<=100 K and >=100 K lines assuming optically thin emission; divide by adopted N(H2)
UCLCHEM three-phase model (diffuse, pre-stellar collapse, warm-up) with updated HOCH2CN network; zeta varied 1-6 times standard
key_parameters: Warm: nH=5e8 cm-3, T up to 160 K; cold: nH=6e6 cm-3, T up to 30 K; G0=1 Habing
assumptions: HOCH2CN forms only on grains; ion-neutral rates assumed like CH3NCO

evidence.quote: cold component (with $T_{\rm ex}$=24$\pm$8$\,$K; see green lines)
$N_{\rm tot}$=(1.8$\pm$0.1)$\times$10$^{15}$$\,$cm$^{-2}$ for the cold and warm components
yielding an HOCH$_2$CN abundance of (6.5$\pm$0.6)$\times$10$^{-11}$ for the warm component
The resulting HOCH$_2$CN abundance for the cold component is therefore (6$\pm$2)$\times$10$^{-10}$.

not_stated_but_needed: CASA version and imaging parameters (weighting, cell, deconvolver, masks)
line-free channels used for continuum subtraction
which dataset covers which lines and the per-dataset beam
priors/initial values and fixed parameters in MADCUBA fits
how the cold-component N and abundance were converted (extended source size handling)
how the warm/cold temperature split was chosen in the rotational diagram (E_up=100 K)
UCLCHEM version and warm-up timescale/heating prescription
score_reason: Public data and software named, but processing and fit settings are sparse and rely on a prior paper.
rediscovery_reason: Data public, numeric results (Tex, N, abundances); recipe moderately complete.
